target.title: fix(memory): accept leading-zero Content-Length on JSON responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where remote memory provider calls would reject successful JSON responses when the provider returned a valid decimal `Content-Length` header with leading zeros, such as `00017`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory-host SDK bounded JSON response reader now accepts digit-only `Content-Length` values while still rejecting empty, non-decimal, and unsafe integer values. This keeps the fix inside the response-size guard used by `postJson` and batch file upload responses without changing request routing, auth, provider selection, or response body limits.

## User Impact

Remote memory and embedding workflows can parse successful JSON responses from providers that emit leading-zero content lengths, while malformed or oversized responses remain blocked at the same guard boundary.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `postJson` and `uploadBatchJsonlFile` accept successful JSON responses with leading-zero `Content-Length` headers while preserving bounded response parsing.
- Current-head proof at `91b4b4062cbf3f0b85bdc6049a51a604ba5ba0f0`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/batch-upload.test.ts` passed with 2 shards and 15 tests.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regressions parse `content-length: 0002` and `content-length: 00017` on successful JSON responses and return the expected `{}` payload and `file_123` upload id.
